title: Conjugate of a Fourier character
statement:
Fix an integer $k \ge 1$, and for $s \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$ let $\chi_s(x) = \omega_k^{s \cdot x}$ be the Fourier character on $\mathbb{Z}_k^n$ indexed by $s$, where $\omega_k = e^{2\pi i/k}$ and $s \cdot x = \sum_{i} s_i x_i \in \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$. Then for every $s, x \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$,
\[
\overline{\chi_s(x)} = \chi_{-s}(x);
\]
that is, complex conjugation of a character amounts to negating its index.
replaced:
For $s, x \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$,
$\overline{\chi_s(x)} = \chi_{-s}(x)$.
Complex conjugation of a character corresponds to negating its index.
